title: docs: add operator runbook links + inline guidance for Dedicated staged rollouts
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Internal-only: Admin tooling now links to the Dedicated staged rollouts operator runbook and includes inline guidance for interpreting gate failures + override requirements.
body:
## Summary
Adds internal runbook links and inline operator guidance in the admin tooling for Dedicated staged rollouts.

This PR is intentionally small, but it unblocks oncall/SRE during beta by making the “what do I do now?” steps available at the point of action (promotion / abort / hold / force-promote).

## Motivation
During beta enablement we saw repeat questions in #eng-oncall and internal support about:
- where the authoritative runbook lives
- what “gate failed: saturation/headroom” means and which dashboards to look at
- when a manual override is acceptable, and what audit reason is required

We already have the runbook + default gate thresholds documented in Confluence, but the admin UI did not surface it. This PR makes those references discoverable without switching contexts.

## What changed
- Admin “Dedicated Pool Rollout” page:
  - Added a prominent internal link to the operator runbook: `Confluence → runbook-dedicated-staged-rollouts-operations`
  - Added inline guidance under Gate Status for common failure categories (latency, error rate, saturation/headroom, GPU health, OOM, 429/drop).
  - Added a short note in the Promote confirmation modal indicating the evaluation window and minimum sample size assumptions (points to Confluence thresholds ADR).
- Admin “Override” actions (force-promote / hold):
  - Added a warning block with required pre-checks and the expectation that an audit reason includes: incident link (if any), dashboard links, and owner ack.
  - Added a link to the audit events spec for staged rollout actions (internal).

No control plane, routing, or telemetry behavior changes.

## Links
- Operator runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/runbook-dedicated-staged-rollouts-operations
- Gate thresholds (internal ADR): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/adr-gate-evaluation-signals-and-thresholds
- SRE SLO alignment doc: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/dedicated-rollout-gates-slo-alignment
- Audit events spec: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/audit-events-for-dedicated-rollout-actions

## Screenshots
- Added “Runbook” link next to Rollout Actions header
- Gate failure help text appears only when gate is FAILED/UNKNOWN (to reduce noise)
- Override modal now includes checklist + link to audit spec

## Testing
- Local: verified links render only for admin users; non-admin sees no internal doc links
- Unit: updated snapshot tests for AdminRolloutPage and PromoteModal
- Manual: verified new copy doesn’t affect action enablement logic (promote/abort/hold)

## Rollout plan
- Safe to ship immediately; internal-only content behind existing admin role checks
- No migrations

## Checklist
- [x] Copy reviewed by SRE
- [x] Security: internal links hidden from customer-facing Console
- [x] Updated snapshots

## Notes
This PR references the current Confluence URLs; if those pages move, the UI will still render but the links will 404. Follow-up task is to route through the internal docs shortlink service once available.
commits: docs(console-admin): add runbook links to Dedicated rollout actions
docs(console-admin): add gate failure inline guidance + dashboard pointers
test: update snapshots for admin rollout page + modals
chore: add internal docs link constants and lint pass
changed_areas: console/admin-backend: expose docs URL config for admin-only UI (no new endpoints)
review_conversation:
Rafael Mendes: Can we make sure the guidance matches the runbook language (esp. saturation/headroom) and doesn’t imply force-promote is “recommended” when metrics are missing? Also please add the oncall playbook link if we have one.

Elliot Price (author): Yep. Updated copy to align with the runbook sections verbatim for each gate category. For missing metrics, wording now says “promotion is blocked; use HOLD and verify telemetry health; force-promote requires admin + audit reason.” We don’t have a stable permalink for the oncall thread yet, so I linked the runbook section “When a gate fails (oncall)” instead.

Allison Grant: +1 on reducing noise. Can we ensure we don’t add stage_id as a clickable filter anywhere? We had cardinality issues; I don’t want UI encouraging ad-hoc queries that explode.

Elliot Price (author): Good call. The inline guidance links to the curated dashboard template and does not add any “open in metrics explorer” deep link. No new filtering controls.

Chloe Martin: Small request: keep Confluence URLs out of customer-facing bundle. Today admin UI is a separate bundle but we’ve had leaks when components were reused.

Elliot Price (author): Added an InternalOnlyLink component that no-ops unless `viewer.is_admin` is true and `environment === 'prod-internal'` (same guard used for other internal tooling). Also added a test asserting link is absent for non-admin.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: For override modal, can we explicitly state the audit reason requirements? We’ve been asked in security review calls to make the operator “intent” clear.

Elliot Price (author): Added a short list: incident reference (if applicable), dashboards reviewed, and owner ack. Also added link to audit event schema doc.

Rafael Mendes: Looks good now. Approved.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; no follow-up revert required.
follow_ups: Route internal doc links via shortlink service (avoid Confluence URL drift)
Add explicit link to a formal oncall playbook once the Confluence page exists (currently embedded in runbook)
